title: count, for_each and the index-shift trap
summary: Many copies of a resource: count for identical ones, for_each for named ones. Why removing the first item of a counted list rebuilds everything after it, and how to migrate to for_each without destroying anything.

steps.title: Many of one thing
body: Two **meta-arguments** make several instances from one block:
for_each = var.services                       # a map: each.key is the name, each.value the object
The difference is the **instance key**: `count` numbers instances by **position**, `for_each` names them by a **key**
(a set of strings or the keys of a map). Keys must be known at plan time, so derive them from inputs, not from
attributes known only after apply. A block can also use `count = var.enabled ? 1 : 0` to be optional.

steps.prompt: Five identical workers behind a load balancer, and a named bucket per site. Which meta-argument for which?
options: `count` for the identical workers, `for_each` for the named buckets
`for_each` for the workers, `count` for the buckets
steps.explain: `count` is fine when instances are interchangeable and you only ever change the number. As soon as instances have an identity (a name, a site, a team), use `for_each`, for the reason on the next card.

steps.title: The index-shift trap, in a real plan
body: `~/infra/sites` made three nginx server blocks with `count` over `["blog", "docs", "shop"]`. The blog moved to a
SaaS platform, so someone removed `"blog"` from the list. Here is the real plan. Instance `[0]` was blog and is now
docs; `[1]` was docs and is now shop; `[2]` no longer exists. Terraform rewrites **every** instance after the removed
one. With files that is noise; with servers or databases it is an outage.

steps.prompt: In that plan, which real objects are rebuilt although nothing about them changed?
options: docs and shop: their configs move to new indexes, so their content changes and forces replacement
all three, plus a new fourth one
steps.explain: Positions shifted: `[0]` gets docs's content, `[1]` gets shop's, `[2]` (the old shop) is destroyed. With `for_each`, removing `"blog"` would destroy exactly `site["blog"]` and leave the others alone.

steps.title: Move to for_each, then remove the blog
prompt: Do ticket WEB-77 (`~/infra/sites/TICKET.txt`) properly: remove the blog **without rebuilding docs or shop**.
1. Change `local_file.site` to `for_each` over the site names (a `set(string)`), with `each.key` instead of
2. Tell Terraform which counted instance is which key, with `moved` blocks.
3. Remove `"blog"`. The plan must destroy only the blog's file and create or replace nothing. Apply.

checks.name: the state uses names
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/sites && terraform state list | sort | tr '\n' ' '
checks.fail: `terraform state list` should show exactly `local_file.site["docs"]` and `local_file.site["shop"]`.

checks.name: docs and shop were never rewritten
checks.fail: `docs.conf` or `shop.conf` was rewritten (its modification time changed). Press Reset scenario; with the right `moved` blocks the plan replaces nothing.

checks.name: the blog is gone
checks.fail: `out/sites/blog.conf` should be gone and `"blog"` removed from the list.

checks.name: for_each, and a clean plan
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/sites && grep -q 'for_each' main.tf && ! grep -q 'count' main.tf && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null
checks.fail: `main.tf` should use `for_each` (no `count` left), and `terraform plan` should show no changes.

hints: `for_each = var.sites` with `type = set(string)`; inside, `each.key` is the site name.
Before removing anything: `moved { from = local_file.site[1]  to = local_file.site["docs"] }` and the same for `[2]` and `"shop"`. Do not move `[0]`: it is the blog, and it should go.
Plan after all three changes: `local_file.site[1]` and `[2]` *have moved*, `local_file.site[0]` *will be destroyed*, nothing else. Then apply.
solution: # One nginx server block per site.
steps.explain: The plan: two *has moved to* notes and one destroy, `local_file.site[0]` (*because resource uses for_each instead of count*). From now on adding or removing a site touches only that site. A safe order in real life is two pull requests: first the migration with `moved` blocks and the same list (plan: no changes), then the removal.

steps.prompt: Keys for `for_each` must be known when planning. Which of these can be the `for_each` set?
items: `{ for s in var.subnets : s.name => s }`
steps.explain: IDs of objects that do not exist yet are *(known after apply)*, so Terraform cannot know which instance keys to plan: *Invalid for_each argument ... The "for_each" set includes values derived from resource attributes that cannot be determined until apply*. Key by names you choose; put the generated IDs in the values instead.

steps.prompt: With this block, what is the address of the instance for the `docs` site?
steps.explain: The map's key is the instance key. In a shell you quote the whole address: `terraform state show 'aws_s3_bucket.site["docs"]'`.
